verdicts.reason: Layer-1 account received the full disputed amount and retains Rs 252,180.68 (66.7% of the dispute). Tainted share is only 3.9%, so the lien targets only the victim's traced money and leaves the vast majority of the account's Rs 65.2 lakh balance untouched.

Taint computation confirms Rs 57,953.27 of victim funds remain in this account; the lien equals the tainted amount and represents a negligible 0.006% of the Rs 9.07 crore balance, so no innocent funds are frozen. Signals (3-year-old personal account, near-zero pass-through, no mule links) are consistent with a genuine endpoint that absorbed stolen money in the ordinary course.

Traced taint of Rs 37,817.81 is confirmed by compute_taint and the lien is only 0.11% of the balance, so the customer's own funds are not affected. Device sharing with another traced account is noted but no mule links exist, consistent with the likely_genuine label.

Compute_taint confirms Rs 14,911.10 of victim money sits in this 6-year-old account with zero tainted outflow, and the lien is just 0.15% of the balance. All signals (low pass-through, no mule-linked devices, long account age) support a genuine endpoint, and the lien only recovers the victim's funds.

Registered merchant with zero pass-through and zero outflow; compute_taint confirms Rs 7,393.01 of victim funds remain, and the lien is a mere 0.02% of the Rs 3.6 crore balance. The 131-device cluster is consistent with a shared merchant terminal, not mule activity.
